sales.title: California reported cannabis sales
sales.description: Retailer-reported cannabis excise-tax sales. Last six published quarters; the full 14-quarter series is in the snapshot. CDTFA update: 27 August 2026.
sales.basis: Calendar quarters, revised administrative returns; not tax revenue or the broader taxable-sales base.

notes.title: California: $3.933bn in calendar 2025
notes.text: Retailer-reported excise-tax cannabis sales fell 6.5% from 2024 in the revised CDTFA series. H1 2026 was $1.977bn, down 0.3% from H1 2025. These nominal dollar measures do not establish unit demand, margins or store performance. Taxable sales also include other retail tangible property and are a different base.

notes.title: A $650m state excise-tax forecast
notes.text: LAO’s September 2, 2026 outlook estimates FY 2025–26 cannabis excise-tax revenue at $630m and forecasts FY 2026–27 at $650m. These July-to-June tax-revenue figures are not retail sales or completed actuals. Q3 2025’s temporary 19% excise rate also breaks simple comparisons; the rate returned to 15% October 1, 2025.

notes.title: U.S. 2025: $28.6–29.6bn estimated
notes.text: First Citizens / Whitney Economics reports this range in its 2026 industry report, compared with approximately $30.1bn for 2024. Detailed tax basis and full market definition were not independently confirmed; the source separates hemp beverages. It is not a government census and cannot support a California market-share calculation. Its URL says 2026 while the body dateline says 2025; that apparent publication typo is unresolved.

nationalContext.title: Federal medical pathway has changed
nationalContext.body: DOJ's April 2026 rule creates a Schedule III pathway for FDA-approved and state-medical-license marijuana, with DEA registration requirements. Other marijuana remains Schedule I. DCC reports implementation underway; an M designation alone does not verify a store's federal registration.

nationalContext.title: Tax effects require activity-level evidence
nationalContext.body: Treasury's April 23 statement planned guidance on Section 280E and mixed activities after medical rescheduling. This edition does not verify subsequent full IRS guidance or estimate any store's tax relief, profitability or valuation.

nationalContext.title: California: adult-use and medical programmes
nationalContext.body: DCC describes adult use for ages 21+ and medicinal access for adults 18+ with a physician recommendation. Local rules can be stricter; state eligibility does not verify a premises license.

nationalContext.title: New York: adult-use programme
nationalContext.body: New York OCM describes adult use for ages 21+ and separately links medical and cannabinoid-hemp programmes.

nationalContext.title: Florida: qualified-patient medical programme
nationalContext.body: Florida OMMU describes qualified-patient access and the licensed Medical Marijuana Treatment Center model. This is a programme example, not a comprehensive Florida legal summary.

nationalContext.title: Hemp is a separate regulatory category
nationalContext.body: Do not add hemp-channel estimates to dispensary sales. DCC currently says licensed California retailers cannot sell hemp while integration rules are being developed; January 1, 2028 integration is future policy, not the October 2026 rule.

caseStudies.title: Lower sales dollars do not establish lower demand
caseStudies.observations: CDTFA's 2025 excise-tax cannabis sales sum to $3.933bn, -6.5% versus 2024. DCC's January 2025 market analysis attributed earlier revenue weakness to lower prices alongside growing quantities.
caseStudies.interpretation: Price pressure is a credible historical explanation to investigate; the dollar series alone cannot establish current unit demand, margins or a particular store's performance.

caseStudies.title: A tax bump can mask softer sales
caseStudies.observations: In Q3 2025, reported cannabis sales fell 6.9% year over year while net excise tax rose 17.3%. The excise rate was 19% that quarter, then returned to 15%.
caseStudies.interpretation: Tax collections are unsuitable as a direct sales-growth proxy. Rate changes, distributor credits and vendor compensation also affect net excise revenue.
caseStudies.status: Derived comparison of official return-period data, with verified policy break
